conclusion: The exact comparison has not been run before: two broad ETFs, one-time CNY 100000 accounts, unchanged R1 candidates and exits, with only entry quantity changed to the frozen 1% planned-risk rule.

literature.title: On the performance of volatility-managed portfolios
literature.method: The paper measures how much daily prices moved during the prior month and uses that to decide the next month's investment amount. Its real-time combinations use an initial 120-month estimation period and then only prior history for the next month, under paper-specific preferences and borrowing limits.
applicable_lessons: separate full-history comparisons from implementable information timing
compare paired methods on the same history
report both risk changes and return costs
inspect instability and concentration across periods
does_not_support: calling this experiment a replication of volatility management

acceptance_recommendations: Keep candidates, exits, timing, products, period, fees, corporate actions, and initial capital unchanged between paired methods.
Use only prior-day equity and information available at the planned entry open.
Count entries where 1% truly reduces quantity, cash caps quantity first, or whole-lot rounding rejects the order.
Report exposure, fees, maximum drawdown, annual wealth contributions, realized results, and unrealized results.
State that gaps and fees can cause actual losses above planned risk.
Treat annual concentration as a historical diagnostic, not future validation.
Do not tune the 1% parameter after seeing results or claim superiority over an untested fixed-reduction control.
